criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: FIVE OF SIX ROUND-3 DEFECTS WERE WORKED AND THREE FULLY TOOK. (1) Frame 4 is a genuine third construction and it works: two portals at one scale, posts sectioned into a lit face and a shaded return, head beam with a lit lip, diamond infill, base plates with a hard contact patch plus a soft throw to frame right, all on one lit slab. It is legible at 290px and it no longer shares the corridor idiom with 1, 6 and 9. THE HALF THAT DID NOT TAKE: the brief says 'a shared dimension line and witness lines across both'. What rendered is TWO SEPARATE dimension lines, one over each portal (left spans x=182 to 670, right spans x=930 to 1420 at display scale), with no shared datum and no numeral, so the frame's whole claim, that the two MEASURE the same, is left to the reader's eye rather than drawn. (2) Frame 3's baffles took: four real value steps now, top land, chamfer, front face, inner face, plus a cast below. (5a) Frame 9's beams took decisively at 14.0 and 9.5 px and both survive the contact sheet. (3) Frame 1's base plates took and are clearly visible under every right-hand post; the head fixings did NOT, and neither did the canopy soffit they attach to (the ribs behind the dek are near-invisible even at 2160px), so the near posts still dissolve upward into nothing. (4) Frame 7 half took: each blank drum now carries its own lateral fall, dark left edge to bright to duller right, which is real. But the apex drift is roughly 8px over 1180px of run, which is imperceptible, and the plate's own lit top edge at y=885 runs the full width at CONSTANT value with no falloff at all, which is the largest element declaring where the light is and it contradicts the falloff the drums were just given. (5b) Frame 9's blanked opening DID NOT TAKE, and darkening the floor and side wall was the wrong half: the defect was never value, it was geometry. The object at (370-820, 1585-1810) still puts a LIGHTER top plane ABOVE a dark face, which is the signature of a box protruding from a wall, not a recess cut into it. It still reads as a plinth. NEW THIS ROUND: frame 9's upper beam is occluded by the 'DALLAS, A DIFFERENT PROGRAM' chip (chip left edge x=805, beam disappears at x=835) and never visibly reaches the aperture plate it terminates on, so the frame's one geometric argument is broken by type on the more important of its two axes. Frame 3's three landings are drawn as hot white blooms BRIGHTER than the coating bloom, so they read as sources, which that frame's own value_structure says they must not. Frame 7's blank lower run reads brighter than the struck run at every size, inverting its own declared focal. Frame 8 delivers no foam: the technique was chosen because 'foam is a material no deck here has touched' and what rendered is dark UI panels with drop shadows on a mottled noise ground. Against this: frame 2 is the best-made frame in fifteen decks' worth of poles, with a real taper, spangle coarsening toward the reader and three collars that are assemblies rather than boxes; frame 6's painted lane edge with a lit lip on the sodium side and a shaded inner face is clean physics. The cap is that frames 8 and 9, the two the argument ENDS on, are the two least made, which is deck 13's and deck 14's avoid_next line unmet for the third consecutive deck.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: All 32 claims are source_type primary_official with fetched URLs and retrieved 2026-09-04. Every numeral traces: '101,306' to c26's raw value 101306 with the separator applied by compute.py; 'over 1.1 million' to c12's quote and attributed on-frame to the bridge director; 'October 2025' to c2; 'SEPT 8TH, 2026' to c24's MatterAgendaDate 2026-09-08; 'May 2026' to c26's date field. The rejected list is unusually disciplined: the Hidalgo attribution is split off the DHS page onto the Census geocoder because the word Hidalgo appears nowhere on the DHS article, the Spanish lane labels are refused because the account never says what the signs said, and 'MARYLAND, ROOFED' is refused as a physical assertion no claim carries. Frame 7's dek closes the deck's most dangerous misread in words ('101,306 pedestrians entered the United States here'). Frame 8's three verbatims each name their speaker (CBP, NEC NSS, S AND T) so a vendor's self-description is not drawn as a government finding. Held below 9 for one thing: frame 1's dek welds a DHS-sourced fact and a Census-sourced county into a single sentence ('ran it for Customs and Border Protection at the Progreso International Bridge in Hidalgo County'), which is exactly the join the run's own rejection note warned about, resolved only by the four claim ids in the footer chip. Separately, and flagged as a LEAD RATHER THAN A FINDING because I could not verify the codepoint with the tools I have: the apostrophe in 'Customs and Border Protection's' on frame 5 should be byte-checked for U+2019 against the straight-quotes-only house rule. I am not asserting it and it is not in hard_fails.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: A Texan learns what happened, who did it, for whom and where: a DHS S&T operational assessment of facial capture on the pedestrian exit lane at the Progreso International Bridge in Hidalgo County, run for CBP, asked for in October 2025, with three solutions from two vendors, an opt-out lane and signs in two languages. That is concrete and it is well sequenced. What the reader cannot do is anything. The only date in the deck belongs to a Dallas briefing on a different program, and frame 9 spends its whole construction saying so, honestly, which is right and is still a dead end. The deeper limit is that the stake itself is abstract by construction: the deck never says what happens to a captured face, because the account does not, so a person walking out of Progreso learns that they were photographed and that no result was published, and nothing about what that costs them. Frame 6 carries the one personal fact a reader could act on, that a citizen could take the other lane, and it is on a past-tense test rather than an ongoing deployment.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The arc is built and the turn lands. Measured [25.0, 15.1, 19.8, 13.6, 96.3, 27.2, 24.7, 13.7, 23.0] puts an 82.7-point junction between frames 4 and 13.6 and 5 at 96.3, exactly at the seam the plan named between the built place and the modelled one, and the ordering the plan asked for survived. Frames 4 and 8 at 13.6 and 13.7 are the two darkest and both are argument frames, which is coherent rather than accidental. The cover earns a swipe and frame 9 lands as a refusal rather than a shrug. THE COST: frames 7 and 8 make the same rhetorical figure back to back, identical objects with one set filled and one set blank, standing for a counted thing beside an uncounted thing. Frame 7's blank drum run and frame 8's five empty cavities are one idea drawn twice, at the exact point the argument is supposed to peak, and neither frame's risk list noticed. The deck also turns at 5 and then goes back to ground at 6, so the brightest frame is not the last thing that changes.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: Clean, plain and on register. 'Judged suitable. Suitable at what?' is the sharpest line in the deck and it is the frame's whole argument in five words. 'One lane was provided for saying no.' and 'They built the lane twice.' are both good and both do work the drawing cannot. No boosterism, no doom, no first person, no em dashes, no colons or semicolons in any dek, ordinal dates month first, straight-looking quotes throughout. Held at 7 because it is a little flat, which is what 7 means here: seven of nine hooks are flat declaratives of near-identical length and cadence, 'The way in has a number' is the weakest of them, and the regional specificity is carried entirely by two place names, Hidalgo County and Progreso, with no Texas vernacular anywhere in the running prose. An outsider could have written eight of these nine deks.

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The register (an optical instrument's interior and the lane it was pointed down) and the palette are genuinely new, and the palette work is unusually rigorous, with six near misses against decks 6 to 14 measured and moved rather than assumed. That is two of the four things this criterion asks about. The other two are repeats, and three of them were named in writing by the two decks immediately before this one. FIRST, the plate primitive is still five of nine. I counted it off the renders: frame 4 (two light plates), frame 6 (two dark chips), frame 7 (two dark chips), frame 8 (three light plates), frame 9 (two dark chips and one light plate). That is the same five-of-nine count deck 13's avoid_next named as 'the deck's real problem', and frame 4's change INVERTED the plate's polarity rather than removing the plate, so the round-4 claim that this 'breaks the five-of-nine repeat of that primitive' is false on the pixels. SECOND, deck 14's avoid_next says 'Seven of nine frames run one type skeleton, so the drawings rotate and the layout does not.' Deck 15 is still seven of nine: only frame 2 departs (a tall left column with the dek dropped to mid-height), and frame 4's move is two labels relocated inside the same grid at the same left margin. The debt is unpaid at the identical number. THIRD, deck median 23.0 is the fifth consecutive dark deck in a 22.2 / 21.2 / 20.4 / 23.0 cluster, and the storyboard's claim that it 'sits in the gap between the priors of 22.2 and 27.7' is 0.8 L* from deck 10. FOURTH and worst, deck 14's angle_note, written yesterday, says in capitals: 'THE NEXT RUN SHOULD PICK A STORY WHERE SOMETHING HAPPENED, not one where a document is quiet.' This deck's declared hero is frame 8, five named absences, and frames 5, 7 and 9 are absence frames too. It is the fifth deck in eight built on what a document does not say. NOT SCORED AS A HARD FAIL: the topic, entities and docket item tx-2026-0120 are new, so this is not 'a topic repeated inside the 30 day window' and I will not stretch that condition to fit.

one_sentence_fix: Rebuild frames 8 and 9 out of the materials they declare rather than repairing them with plates, because one change fixes four separate findings at once: frame 8's foam is absent and the frame renders as dark UI panels, frame 9's blanked opening is still a lit-top-plane-over-dark-face and so still reads as a plinth, those two frames are the least made in the deck for the third consecutive deck against deck 13's and deck 14's avoid_next, and the five-of-nine plate count that the frame 4 repair was supposed to break is carried by exactly those two frames plus 6 and 7.
